protocol: MEMRA_PP_ONLY interleaved x2 rounds, one session, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2, GPUs 0/1/4-7 running other lanes' load throughout; tree=lane/sk-ncu (restructure/public-split tip 6362507c) built on-box cuda-13.3.1

note: cublas +1.9-2.4% e2e both rounds — reproduces the 8380-vs-7990 direction within-session (those were another session; clock-drift law: no cross-session absolute comparison)

HEADLINE: cublas grouped on H100 dispatches a CUTLASS sm_80-class mma.sync (s16816=m16n8k16) GROUPED kernel — NOT wgmma/TMA. Same instruction class as our sk kernel; the difference is tile (128x64, BK=64, 3-stage) + persistent problem-visitor scheduling. Mode 1 also pays h2f_rows_scale 240x45.1us (5.4ms/prime) + ~120 stream syncs/prime (cuStreamSynchronize med 1.22ms) and still nets +2% e2e.

sk 1.32x SLOWER per GEMM call on H100 at wild clocks; 5090 receipt was sk 1.61ms vs cublas 1.80ms (sk 1.12x FASTER). GEMM stage delta ~18ms/prime for mode 1, minus mode-1 taxes ~5.4ms h2f + sync gaps = the observed ~2% e2e win.

sk is L2-THROUGHPUT-BOUND (75-88% L2 SOL, DRAM only 27-32%, tensor/SM 15-16%): BM=32 re-fetches each expert W tile from L2 once per 32 output rows. Occupancy register-capped at 31%; schedulers idle 83-85% of cycles. grid.y sized for max_m=~1120-1152 rows while avg group m is ~65 (derived: ~250 active groups of 256 experts) -> 92% of the 274-290k blocks are early-exit churn on the big-grid calls.

grid: (264,1,1)x(128,1,1) PERSISTENT = 2 CTAs/SM x 132 SMs, waves=1, problem-visitor enumerates tiles
note: cutlass saturates NOTHING (L2 20-31%, DRAM 19-28%, SM 10-14%) at HALF sk's occupancy — a latency-tolerant design: BM=128 reads each W tile from L2 4x less often than BM=32, BK=64 3-stage cp.async pipeline + big per-warp ILP hides latency with only 8 warps/SM. CAVEAT: at ncu-locked base clock cutlass avg 779us vs sk 662us (ordering flips vs wild-clock nsys 486 vs 640) — cutlass's win rides boost clocks + un-saturated data paths; the utilization percentages are the evidence here, wild-clock ordering comes from the nsys rows.

find: why cublas grouped beats sk on H100 while sk won the 5090 GEMM stage
detail: REFUTED: 'cublas picks a fundamentally better algo (wgmma/TMA)' — the dispatched kernel is cutlass_80 s16816 = the same mma.sync.m16n8k16 class as sk. CONFIRMED mechanism: sk's BM=32xBN=64 tile is L2-traffic-bound on H100 — each expert's W slice is re-read from L2 per 32-row m-tile, and q35's skewed routing (max group ~1152 rows vs ~65 avg) makes the hot groups pay 36 W re-reads vs cutlass's 9 (BM=128 = 4x fewer). H100's 132 SMs multiply aggregate L2 demand past the L2's serve rate (sk sits at 75-88% L2 SOL = the wall), while its 3.35TB/s HBM stays at ~30%. On the 5090 (82 SMs, 858GB/s) the same kernel runs against the DRAM roofline where W streams once either way — there sk's zero-sync single launch + folded f32-C h2f won the stage. Secondary sk taxes on H100: register-capped 31% occupancy, and 92% early-exit block churn from grid.y=ceil(max_m/32) under 17x routing skew.

(1) TILE: add a BM=128/BN=64/BK=64 3-stage instantiation (sm_80-portable, mma.sync — no wgmma needed to reach cublas's H100 number; cublas itself doesn't use it) selected when max_m is large (prefill); keep 32x64 for small-m shapes. This is the 4x L2-traffic lever = the whole 1.32x gap and more. (2) SCHEDULING: replace grid.y=ceil(max_m/32) with persistent CTAs + a device tile-list/problem-visitor (cutlass runs 264 CTAs = 2/SM, waves=1, zero early-exit; sk launches 290k blocks, ~92% exit early under routing skew). Persistent-CTA count target: 2/SM with the big tile (reg/smem limited), it needs no more. (3) REGISTERS: with the big tile expect ~200 regs — occupancy 12.5% is FINE if the pipeline is 3+ stages deep (cutlass proves it); do not chase occupancy, chase pipeline depth. (4) wgmma port: NOT the mechanism of the current loss — defer; it remains Hopper-gated headroom (SM SOL is 10-16% everywhere, compute ceiling far away; the war is in the data path). WIN CONDITION: sk at GEMM parity (~486us/call) keeps its structural edge (no h2f pass 5.4ms/prime, zero per-projection syncs) -> mode 2 should flip to the H100 winner by roughly the current gap reversed (~+18ms GEMM saved + 5.4ms h2f kept dead per prime).

find: ncu operational gotchas for this lane
detail: (a) GPU perf counters need sudo on this box (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM otherwise); (b) ncu kernel-name filter matches the demangled BASE name — the cutlass kernel is 'Kernel2', regex:cutlass matches nothing, use regex:Kernel2; (c) full section sets = 20 replay passes/launch (~2.5min each on this kernel) — SpeedOfLight+Occupancy+SchedulerStats+LaunchStats (9 passes) is the budget set; (d) q35 dims read off the launch grids: n_expert=256 (grid.z 245-252 active), n_ff_exp=512 (gate/up grid.x=8), n_embd=2048 (down grid.x=32).
